<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | Confirmed, bounded correctness defect |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium |
| Task Type | Targeted verification-preflight fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

Review finding `INIT-MONO-001` claims that malformed root `package.json` test metadata can cause verification to select a valid nested package instead of failing closed.

### What We Found

`preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` resolves and validates the configured `cwd`, then validates the package script at that exact directory. Missing, non-object, non-string, and blank script values are rejected by `assertPackageScript`. Existing coverage proves that a root command does not silently use a nested package when the root has no `test` script.

However, `packageScriptName` only inspects `argv[1]`. Package-manager selectors placed before the subcommand (for example `npm --prefix web test` or `npm --workspace web test`) return no script name, so preflight skips package metadata validation even though the package manager can execute `test` from the nested package while the process cwd remains the repository root. This is the remaining bypass for malformed root metadata.

### Root Cause

The package-manager argument parser assumes the script subcommand is always the second argv element. It does not recognize a script subcommand after supported selector/options, so the static package-script assertion can be bypassed.

### Affected Files

| Path | Change Needed |
|---|---|
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Parse script subcommands after package-manager options so nested selectors cannot bypass root metadata validation. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Add malformed-root and selector regression cases. |

### Evidence

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:57-59` validates a package only when `packageScriptName` returns a script.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:119-129` reads only `argv[1]`, allowing selector-before-command forms to return `undefined`.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:161-173` correctly treats non-object script maps and non-string/blank values as invalid once validation is reached.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts:63-83` covers a missing root script with a valid nested package, but not malformed metadata or selector-before-command forms.
- `README.md` requires monorepo checks to bind `cwd` to the owning package and says invalid package scripts fail closed; CI-only verification is represented by an empty command map.

### History Findings

The supplied issue identifies source PR #110 and finding `INIT-MONO-001`; its evidence says a prior remediation treated malformed `scripts.test` values as invalid and added regression coverage. The current branch contains the direct-cwd validation portion, but the command parser still leaves an option-before-subcommand bypass. No unrelated history or scope is required.

### Recommendation

Keep the exact-cwd contract and fail-closed behavior. Extend the small package-manager parser to locate direct `test`/`run`/`run-script` subcommands after recognized selector/options, then assert the script in the configured cwd. Add focused tests proving malformed root metadata is rejected even when a nested package has a valid script, while an explicitly configured nested cwd remains valid. Users needing CI-only verification should remove local commands rather than rely on malformed package metadata.

### Related Issues

- Source review finding: `INIT-MONO-001` from PR #110.
- Source issue: #94.
- Current remediation issue: #114.

### Decomposition Assessment

This is a single cohesive change across one adapter and its focused test. No decomposition is warranted.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Recognize package-manager script commands after supported selector/options without selecting a different cwd implicitly.
- [ ] Reject malformed root `scripts.test` values even when a nested package has a valid test script.
- [ ] Preserve valid explicitly configured nested-package verification.
- [ ] Add focused regression coverage and pass the required `check` verification.
- [ ] Re-review the exact remediation head.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Close the package-manager option-before-subcommand bypass so required local verification cannot execute a nested package while malformed root test metadata is ignored. Preserve the existing explicit-`cwd` monorepo contract and fail-closed behavior.

### Allowed Paths

| Path | Allowed Scope |
|---|---|
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Package-manager script-command detection and the associated validation path only. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Focused fixture/assertion coverage for malformed root metadata, selector options, and explicit nested cwd behavior. |

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test`/`run`/`run-script` invocations preceded by supported package-manager options are recognized for package-script validation.
- [ ] A malformed or blank root `scripts.test` value fails closed even when a nested package defines a valid `test` script.
- [ ] An explicitly configured nested package cwd with a valid script remains accepted.
- [ ] Existing executable, path, and package-manifest safety checks remain unchanged.
- [ ] The required `check` verification passes.

### Invariants

- Verification executes only the tracked argv and resolved repository-relative cwd.
- No implicit package discovery or nested-package fallback is introduced.
- CI-only verification remains the explicit empty-command configuration.
- Symlink escapes, control directories, missing manifests, invalid JSON, and invalid script values continue to fail closed.
- No policy, workflow authority, GitHub artifact, or UX behavior changes.

### Deliverables

1. A small deterministic parser update that recognizes package-manager script commands after supported options without selecting a cwd.
2. Focused regression tests with a malformed root manifest and a valid nested manifest.

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change `.forge/config.json`, policy schemas, workflow state, GitHub adapters, review behavior, or package scripts.
- Do not execute verification commands during preflight.
- Do not broaden package-manager support beyond the targeted parser behavior.
- Do not add dependencies or modify unrelated tests/documentation.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

- Issue #114 tracks source finding `INIT-MONO-001` from PR #110 / source issue #94.
- The current branch already validates the manifest at the exact configured cwd and rejects non-string/blank script values when the script is recognized.
- The remaining defect is limited to command parsing when package-manager selectors occur before the script subcommand.

### Callers And Data Flow

- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` iterates tracked required commands.
- `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory` canonicalizes the repository-relative cwd and rejects escapes/control directories.
- `packageScriptName` decides whether package metadata must be checked.
- `assertPackageScript` reads only `<resolved cwd>/package.json` and validates the requested script.
- The child `forge_verify` tool separately resolves the same tracked cwd before executing argv; this change only closes the preflight gap.

### CI Surface

- Required bound verification command: `check` → `npm run check` from repository root.
- GitHub CI remains authoritative after PR creation; no new local command is introduced.

### Prior Findings

- `INIT-MONO-001`: malformed root test metadata could select a nested package.
- Existing regression coverage verifies missing root script plus valid nested package, but not malformed values or selector-before-command argv.

### Hazards

- Do not scan for or infer a nested package; explicit `cwd` is the only package selection mechanism.
- Do not treat arbitrary non-script package-manager subcommands as package scripts.
- Preserve `npm run <script>` argument handling and platform executable lookup.
- Keep fixture manifests private and temporary; do not add repository package metadata.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

| Step | Action | Acceptance Checks |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Update `packageScriptName` to recognize the targeted script subcommands after supported package-manager option forms while retaining direct `test`, `run`, and `run-script` behavior. | AC-1, AC-2 |
| 2 | Extend the temporary preflight fixture so the root manifest carries malformed `scripts.test` metadata while the nested package carries a valid test script; add selector-before-command rejection assertions. | AC-2 |
| 3 | Retain and exercise the explicit nested cwd success case, plus existing path/executable safety cases. | AC-3, AC-4 |
| 4 | Review the bounded diff, run the required `check` command through `forge_verify`, and commit only the contracted files. | AC-5 |

### Expected Result

The preflight either validates the script in the exact configured cwd or fails closed. It never uses a nested package merely because package-manager argv options point there.
